## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sahetukaduka* is a section of the *Paṭṭhāna* in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka of the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. In modern analysis, it is translated as "The Dyad 'accompanied by root, and unaccompanied by root'" and constitutes the second dyad chapter in the origination of dyads (*duka-paṭṭhāna*), which encompasses one hundred dyadic chapters [Nyanatiloka 1938].
According to DharmaNexus, the text exhibits extensive internal text reuse across the Pali Abhidhamma, sharing 716 matching passages with 85 other Pali texts, particularly other treatises of the *Paṭṭhāna* [DharmaNexus]. Its most substantial overlaps occur with *Tika Hetuduka* (Patthana 4.1; 56 matches), *Hetugocchaka* (Patthana 2.1; 53 matches), *Hetuduka, Duka* (Patthana 6.1; 42 matches), and *Kusalattika, Hetugocchaka* (Patthana 4.2; 31 matches) [DharmaNexus]. Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus records any external cross-language parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan collections [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
